metaDescription: PSB Tm9 (CL 143 0 10 3 1 10) tomato is a tomato variety for Luzon and Mindanao. About 61 days to harvest, 17.9 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: PSB Tm9 (CL 143 0 10 3 1 10) is a registered tomato variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1999 as NSIC 1999 Tm 09. It takes about 61 days from transplanting to the first harvest, with 17.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

PSB Tm9 (CL 143 0 10 3 1 10) tomato takes about 61 days from transplanting to the first harvest. That is 9.6 days faster than the average of the 20 tomato varieties with a day count, 70.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 17.9 t/ha trails the average of its group, 20.91. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

blocks.text: It was weak against fusarium wilt, so scout for it from the early weeks. Read up on [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt).

The pests and diseases that hit tomato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [late blight](/diseases/late-blight), [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A fruit weighs about 30 grams. It is semi globe.
Where and when to plant PSB Tm9 (CL 143 0 10 3 1 10) tomato

It is recommended for Luzon and Mindanao in the wet season. Bacterial wilt kills more lowland tomato than any other disease, so in the wet season pick a variety rated resistant to it. Choose a firm, oblong fruit if you sell to a far market, and a round, juicy one for fresh sale nearby. Heat tolerant hybrids set fruit in the hot months, when open pollinated tomatoes often drop their flowers. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 61 days from transplanting to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 17.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for Luzon and Mindanao in the wet season. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
